text.en: Meena looked at a photo and its enlarged print. "The shape is the same, only bigger," she said.

Similar figures have the same shape but not always the same size. The Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales) says a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. Its converse is also true, and the angle bisector theorem divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides.
Triangles are similar by the AA, SSS and SAS criteria. The ratio of the areas of similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides. The Pythagoras theorem and its converse are proved with similar triangles.
A tangent touches a circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius there. Two tangents drawn from an outside point are equal in length, and the tangent-chord and alternate segment theorems follow. Constructions of tangents and of triangles with given conditions use a ruler and a compass.

board.text: Match the vertices before comparing sides

text.en: A triangle with sides three, four and five is similar to a triangle with sides six, eight and ten. Every side in the second triangle is twice as long.

board.text: Same scale factor on all sides

text.en: If two angles of one triangle match two angles of a second triangle, the third angles match too. That is enough to prove similarity.
Compare all three corresponding side ratios. If they are equal, the triangles are similar.
For side-angle-side similarity, the matching angles lie between the two pairs of sides with equal ratios.

board.text: SAS: a matching angle between proportional sides

text.en: Draw D on AB and E on AC of triangle ABC. When DE is parallel to BC, AD over DB equals AE over EC.

board.text: If DE ∥ BC, the side parts are proportional

text.en: If AD is two and DB is four, the side-part ratio is one half. If AE is three, EC must be six.
If D and E divide the sides in the same ratio, the converse tells us that DE is parallel to the third side.

board.text: Converse: matching side parts give a parallel line

text.en: Draw the bisector of angle A to point D on BC. Then BD over DC equals AB over AC. The two parts of BC need not have the same length.

board.text: An angle bisector splits the angle equally

text.en: If BC is fifteen units, divide it into five equal shares. Give BD two shares, or six units, and DC three shares, or nine units.
Doubling each side doubles each height. Base times height therefore grows by four, so the area of the similar triangle is four times as large.

board.text: Side factor k becomes area factor k²

text.en: In a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares on the two shorter sides.

board.text: In a right triangle: a² + b² = c²

text.en: The sum twenty-five plus one hundred and forty-four is one hundred and sixty-nine. The hypotenuse is thirteen units.
For sides six, eight and ten, the squares of the two shorter sides sum to the square of ten. The angle opposite ten is a right angle.

board.text: Converse tests a possible right angle

text.en: Join the centre O to the point T where the tangent touches. OT and the tangent meet at right angles.

board.text: A tangent and the radius meet at 90°

text.en: If OT is five and the external distance OP is thirteen, use Pythagoras. PT is the square root of one hundred and sixty-nine minus twenty-five, so PT is twelve.
Draw another tangent from P touching at U. The lengths PT and PU match. They are measured from P to the two touching points.

board.text: Tangent segments from one point have equal lengths

text.en: At a point of tangency, the angle between a tangent ray and a chord equals the angle made by the chord in the alternate segment.

board.text: The alternate segment angle lies across the chord

text.en: The three medians of a triangle are concurrent at the centroid. A median runs from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

board.text: Concurrent lines pass through one point

text.en: In triangle ABC, let D, E and F lie on BC, CA and AB. The lines AD, BE and CF meet at one point when BD over DC times CE over EA times AF over FB equals one.
With midpoint ratios of one, one and one, their product is one. That explains why the three medians meet at a single point.
Use the same three side ratios with one point on an extension. If the product of their positive lengths is one, the three points are on a straight line.

problem.en: In a right triangle the legs are 3 and 4. Find the hypotenuse.

text.en: Use Pythagoras: c^2 = 3^2 + 4^2.

problem.en: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC. If DE is parallel to BC, AD = 4, DB = 6 and AE = 8, find EC.

text.en: Use AD/DB = AE/EC.

why.en: The parallel segment divides both sides in the same ratio.

problem.en: A circle has radius 5 cm. A point P lies 13 cm from its centre. Find the length of a tangent segment from P.

text.en: Draw the radius to the contact point. It is perpendicular to the tangent.

why.en: The centre, contact point and P form a right triangle.

text.en: Tangent length = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm.

why.en: The centre-to-point length is the hypotenuse.

problem.en: For internal points D, E and F, suppose BD/DC = 2 and CE/EA = 3. Find AF/FB so the three cevians meet.

text.en: Use Ceva’s product 2 × 3 × AF/FB = 1.

why.en: All three ratios are taken in the same cyclic order.

text.en: AF/FB = 1/6.

why.en: The first two ratios multiply to 6, so divide 1 by 6.

prompt.en: A friend says Similar triangles always have equal areas. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: They have the same shape, not always the same size.
Area ratio is the square of the side ratio.

points.en: Thales: a parallel line divides sides proportionally.
Tangents from a point are equal.
Tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
